about.title: Westlake Village Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Workplace injuries in Westlake Village happen in offices, retail spaces, and on the roads that connect this Los Angeles County community, including Lindero Canyon Road and Triunfo Canyon Road corridors where delivery and service vehicles travel daily. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive path for benefits from your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. This matters in a small city like Westlake Village, where many workers commute through shared job sites and business parks with multiple contractors present. LawProactive doesn't practice law directly; we're a free service that connects injured workers with an independent attorney who can look at the full picture of what happened and explain your options at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Workers in Westlake Village Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Workers' Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: California generally treats workers' comp as your exclusive remedy against your employer, but that doesn't rule out a separate claim against a negligent third party. An independent attorney can help sort out which path — or both — applies to your situation.

items.title: Protecting Your Rights After Reporting an Injury
items.desc: You have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and California law prohibits retaliation for doing so. If you've faced pushback after reporting, an attorney in our network can talk through what protections you have.

items.title: Watching the Clock on Third-Party Deadlines
items.desc: If a third party contributed to your injury, that separate claim generally carries a two-year deadline in California. Connecting early with an attorney helps make sure that window doesn't close while you're focused on recovery.

items.question: I already filed a workers' comp claim in Westlake Village. Can I still pursue something else?
items.answer: Yes, in many cases. Workers' comp and a third-party claim aren't mutually exclusive under California law. If someone other than your employer contributed to your injury, an independent attorney can evaluate whether a separate claim makes sense alongside your existing workers' comp benefits.

items.question: My injury happened while driving for work near Agoura Road. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. If another driver was involved in the collision, that could open the door to a third-party injury claim in addition to any workers' comp benefits you're entitled to. An attorney can review the details of the crash to see how it fits together.

items.question: What does LawProactive actually do?
items.answer: We're a free connection service, not a law firm. We match injured workers in Westlake Village with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery, so you can get answers without upfront cost.
